props.gloss_en: Beit Shammai: an egg laid on Yom Tov may be eaten
Beit Hillel: an egg laid on Yom Tov may not be eaten

entertained: the mishnah concerns a hen kept for eating. Refuted in place: the egg would be food-that-separated, and BH would have no ground. Content deliberately withheld: the same construal RETURNS at 2b.8 inside Rabbah's hakhana frame, and sharing content atoms would let this reductio shadow his revival
the standing okimta of stage 1: the mishnah concerns a hen kept for laying, so the egg-prohibition is a muktzeh matter -- Rav Nachman affirms it (לעולם, 2a.7); genuinely defeated by the 2b.4 kushya
the working assumption: even one who permits muktzeh forbids nolad -- so BS's leniency has no tannaitic home. Abandoned when Rav Nachman splits the positions (2a.7)
Rav Nachman's account: BH forbid the egg as nolad, and nolad rides with muktzeh -- whoever holds the one holds the other
Rav Nachman's mapping: Beit Shammai follow R' Shimon, who rejects muktzeh (and so nolad)
Rav Nachman's mapping: Beit Hillel follow R' Yehuda, who holds muktzeh (and so nolad)

Rav Nachman's other memra (on the bones-and-shells mishnah): BS like R' Yehuda, BH like R' Shimon -- the contradicting source of the 2a.8 objection. Content deliberately withheld (header): after 2a.10 both mappings stand domain-scoped
it is Rabbi who fixed the anonymous mishnah -- one author behind both stams, which is what makes the Shabbat/YT asymmetry a question
Rabbah's okimta: a hen kept for eating, on a Yom Tov that falls after Shabbat -- the prohibition is a hakhana matter
Rabbah's account: the egg was completed yesterday (on Shabbat), and Shabbat may not prepare for Yom Tov
Rabbah's hakhana derasha: a weekday prepares for Shabbat and for Yom Tov; neither holy day prepares for the other. SCOPE-REJECTED at 3a.4 (הכנה לית להו) by deny commits, never globally defeated

Rabbah's defence-prop: the egg is forbidden on an ordinary Yom Tov as a decree, lest one permit it on a YT after Shabbat -- given prop-hood so the 2b.12 attack on THIS move can be encoded without attacking an answer (the answers-cannot-be-attacked gap, routed around)
and the mirror decree for an ordinary Shabbat
the baraita: complete eggs found in a slaughtered hen may be eaten on Yom Tov -- no decree was made against them
Rabbah's deflection-ground as a rule: the rabbis decline the proposed decree-ground -- eggs complete in the mother are uncommon, and no decree is made for the uncommon
Rav Yosef's account: the egg is forbidden as a decree assimilating it to fruit that falls on Yom Tov (itself guarded lest one climb and pluck, 3a.1)
R' Yitzchak's account: the egg is forbidden as a decree assimilating it to liquids that flowed of themselves (guarded lest one squeeze, 3a.3)

objections.gloss_en: ומי אמר רב נחמן הכי? והתנן: בית שמאי אומרים מגביהין מעל השלחן עצמות וקליפין... ואמר רב נחמן: אנו אין לנו אלא ב"ש כרבי יהודה וב"ה כר"ש! (equally strikes p_bs_kershimon -- header)

answered_by.gloss_en: גבי שבת דסתם לן תנא כר"ש (מחתכין את הדלועין) מוקים לה לב"ה כר"ש; אבל גבי יו"ט דסתם לן תנא כרבי יהודה (אין מבקעין עצים) מוקים לה לב"ה כרבי יהודה (2a.10-2b.1)

objections.gloss_en: במאי אוקימתא -- בתרנגולת העומדת לגדל ביצים ומשום מוקצה. אי הכי, אדמיפלגי בביצה לפלגו בתרנגולת! The defence להודיעך כחן דב"ש דבנולד שרי (2b.5) is rebutted: ולפלוגי בתרנגולת להודיעך כחן דב"ה! וכי תימא כח דהתירא עדיף -- ונפלוג בתרוייהו: תרנגולת העומדת לגדל ביצים היא וביצתה (2b.6-7). No answer follows; אלא אמר רבה (2b.8)
ומי גזרינן? והתניא: השוחט את התרנגולת ומצא בה ביצים גמורות -- מותרות לאכלן ביום טוב. ואם איתא, לגזר משום הנך דמתילדן ביומיהן!

answered_by.gloss_en: ביצים גמורות במעי אמן מילתא דלא שכיחא היא, ומילתא דלא שכיחא לא גזרו בה רבנן (= p_lo_gazru_delo_shechicha)
